To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a naturally occurring monocloal antibody (SAG-3) from an NZB mice, which is similar to NTA in its serology, is capable of eliminating the proliferative response of T cells to Con-A, and of reducing their capacity to respond to mitogens and alloantigens in vitro.

the naturally occurring monocloncal antibody SAG-3 is reactive against T cells which possess both Lyt-2 and L3T-4 antigens, and that this antibody has the capacity to eliminate the proliferative response of T cells to mitogens and to suppress the generation and activity of CTL and helper T cells.
SAG-3 reacts with a subset of functional T cells, and that the antibody appears to have a preferential specificity for T cells bearing Lyt-2 antigens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional characterization of a monoclonal antibody which is reactive with a subset of functional T lymphocytes.
the functional characterization of S.A.G.3, an NTA-like monoclonal antibody.
the in vitro functional characterization of a naturally occurring monocional antibody (SAG-3) in NZB mice, which possesses the serologic characteristics of serum thymocytotic autoantibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SAG-3 is a monoclonal antibody which reacts with functional thymocytolytic T cells, which may play an important role in the T cell mediated autoimmunity observed in NZB mice.
the functional characteristics of SAG- 3 are similar, but not identical, to those of serum-NTAs.
SAG-3 is a naturally occurring monocloantibody which reacts with functional T cell subsets in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SAG-3 is a monoclonal antibody which is reactive with a population of thymocytes and T cells which are involved in the regulation of the T cell mediated proliferative and cytolytic responses.
SAG-3 is reactive against a subset of T cells which possess the capacity to respond to mitogenic and allogenic stimuli and to generate primary and secondary CTL responses.
SAG-3 is a functional monoclonal NTA which is reactive against T cells which express the Lyt-2 and L3T 4 surface markers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SAG-3, a naturally occurring monocloonal antibody, can be used to characterize the functional characteristics of NTA in NZB mice and to study the role of NTA in the immune system.

SAG-3 is a monoclonal antibody with a specificity towards functional T cell subsets, which is not reactive against suppressor T cells, and that SAG-2, a monoclonal anti-Lyt-2 antibody, can be used to generate a monoclonal NTA.
SAG-3, like NTA, is a naturally occurring autoantibody that is specific for T cells.
